title: Elements of Communication
notes: A communication system moves a message from one place to another. The information source produces the message, which may be speech, music or data.
The transmitter converts that message into a signal that can travel. For radio this includes modulation, placing the message onto a high-frequency carrier so that the antenna can be a practical size.
The channel is the path: a wire, an optical fibre, or free space. Noise, which is unwanted electrical energy, is added along the channel and is not part of the message.
The receiver undoes the transmitter's work. It amplifies the weak signal and demodulates it, recovering a copy of the original message for the listener or the display.
Attenuation is the weakening of the signal with distance. Amplifiers along a long channel restore the level, but they cannot perfectly remove noise that was added earlier.
Bandwidth is the range of frequencies the message or the channel occupies. A wider message, such as video, needs a wider channel than speech.

exercises.question: A speech signal is to be sent by radio. Put the blocks in order and say where noise is added.
steps: The information source is the speaker, turned into an electrical message by a microphone.
The transmitter modulates that message onto a radio-frequency carrier and feeds an antenna.
The channel is free space, and noise is added there.
The receiver antenna, amplifier and demodulator recover the speech.
The order is source, transmitter, channel, receiver.
exercises.answer: Source, transmitter, channel, receiver. Noise is added in the channel.
